message:
Please review the following document.

<document>
# 2027 Customer Support Hiring Plan

**To:** Chief Operating Officer | **From:** Support Operations | **Date:** 13 November 2026

**Decision requested:** Approve 12 net new agents in two phases: 8 starting January 11 and 4 starting in September. Separately, approve a capped vendor overflow budget for tax season.

## Recommendation

| Item | Timing | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 8 net new agents | Jan 11 class | At least 6 bilingual English/Spanish |
| 4 net new agents | Sept class | Confirmed at a July review of Q2 self-service results |
| Backfills | Monthly, 1–3 per class | Sized to actual attrition; bilingual preferred |
| Vendor overflow | Feb–Apr | Non-complaint tickets, capped at ~$150k |

The 12 net hires would cost about **$610k in 2027**, compared with $816k for 12 full-year positions.

## Demand

- **Average month in 2027:** 31,000 × 1.35 (user growth) × 0.88 (help-centre effect) ≈ **36,800 tickets**. At 740 tickets per agent, that needs about 50 fully productive agents.
- **Complaint rule:** Adding 6 minutes to about 3,300 complaint tickets a month uses about 330 agent-hours, or roughly 2.4 agents (assuming 140 productive hours per agent-month).
- **Steady-state need:** about 52 agents. Our 42 plus 12 gives 54, which covers it.

The average hides the shape of the year:

- **Tax season (Feb–Apr)** runs at about 51,600 tickets a month and needs about 70 agents. No hiring plan closes this gap. Even the January 11 class only reaches full productivity on March 22.
- **The other nine months** run about 13% below average. They need about 45 agents early in the year, rising toward 52 by Q4 as users grow.

Hiring all 12 in Q1 would leave us 6–8 agents overstaffed through mid-year and still short during tax season.

## Why this phasing

- **January (8):** Our current capacity (42 × 740 = 31,080 tickets) equals 2026 average demand, so we have no slack today. These hires will be productive before the April 1 complaint rule takes effect.
- **September (4):** These agents will be fully productive by mid-November, ahead of Q4 growth and the 2028 tax season. Waiting also shows us whether dispute tracking and card replacement reduce volume. If they do, we may need fewer.
- **Vendor for the peak:** Even after the January class, we will be short about 16,000–17,500 tickets a month. At $4.10 per ticket, the vendor is cheaper than an in-house agent (about $7.66 per ticket) for a three-month spike. Complaints must stay in-house. Capping the vendor at about 36,000 tickets means we absorb the rest as longer waits, as we did in 2026, when peak capacity was about 28% below demand.

## Spanish coverage

Spanish is 18% of volume, about 6,600 tickets a month in 2027. That needs about 9 bilingual agents, and we have 4, which explains why Spanish waits are 3.4 times longer. Weighting the January class toward bilingual hires brings us to about 10 bilingual agents by Q2. Offers must go out by mid-December, so recruiting should start bilingual sourcing now.

## Attrition is the larger risk

At 38% attrition, we lose about 18 agents a year. That is more than the net growth requested here, and each replacement loses about 5 weeks of productivity while ramping up. Exit interviews cite night-shift scheduling and below-market pay. I will bring a proposal in Q1 covering a night-shift differential or rotation and a pay benchmark. Cutting attrition to 28% would avoid about 5 replacement hires a year.

## Assumptions to confirm

- Backfills are funded within the existing 42 positions, not from the 12.
- 35% user growth means the 2027 average compared with the 2026 average.
- The 12% help-centre reduction will persist.
- Agents have about 140 productive hours per month.

---

##
</document>
response:
# Review: 2027 Customer Support Hiring Plan

This is a strong memo. The recommendation comes first, the phasing argument is clear, and almost every figure checks out. The main gaps are an incomplete cost picture, a thin capacity margin once attrition is counted, and one demand figure that doesn't reconcile.

## Arithmetic check

I verified these figures and they're internally consistent:

| Claim | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 36,800 avg tickets | 31,000 × 1.35 × 0.88 = 36,828 | ✅ |
| ~50 agents | 36,828 / 740 = 49.8 | ✅ |
| Complaint load 2.4 agents | 3,300 × 6 min = 330 h; / 140 = 2.36 | ✅ |
| ~70 agents at peak | 51,600 / 740 = 69.7 | ✅ |
| Off-peak 13% below avg | (441,600 − 154,800) / 9 = 31,867, which is 13.4% below | ✅ |
| $610k vs $816k | $68k/agent; 8 × ~0.96 yr + 4 × ~0.33 yr ≈ $613k | ✅ |
| $7.66/ticket in-house | $68k / 12 / 740 = $7.66 | ✅ |
| Vendor cap ~$150k | 36,000 × $4.10 = $147.6k | ✅ |
| 2026 peak 28% short | 2026 peak ≈ 43,400 vs 31,080 capacity → 28.4% | ✅ |
| Spanish need ~9 | 36,800 × 18% = 6,624; / 740 = 8.95 | ✅ |
| Jan 11 → Mar 22 | Both Mondays, 10 weeks apart | ✅ |
| Attrition ~18/yr; 28% saves ~5 | 38% × ~48 avg headcount ≈ 18; 10 pts × 48 ≈ 5 | ✅ |

## Substantive issues

**1. The total 2027 cost is missing.** The memo gives $610k for hires and ~$150k for the vendor separately, but never adds them. The COO will want to see **~$760k incremental**, plus any recruiting or training costs. Consider adding a one-line total under the Recommendation table.

**2. The off-peak staffing figures don't reconcile.** Off-peak demand averages ~31,900 tickets/month, or **~43 agents** (~45.5 including the complaint rule). The memo says need is "about 45 early, rising toward 52 by Q4," which implies an average of roughly 48. Either the early-year figure is too high or the growth curve is steeper than shown. Since the "6–8 overstaffed" argument depends on these numbers, it's worth tightening them.

**3. Attrition ramp loss uses up the cushion.** The memo shows 54 agents against a need of 52. But 18 replacements × 5 lost weeks ≈ 90 agent-weeks, or **~1.7 FTE of lost capacity**. Monthly backfill classes also mean vacancies sit open for weeks before a replacement starts. In practice the margin is close to zero. That strengthens your attrition section, so say it explicitly: "after ramp losses, effective capacity is about 52, with no margin."

**4. It's unclear whether the September 4 are approved now or later.** The decision line asks to "approve 12," but the table says the September class is "confirmed at a July review." State which you want, for example: "Approve 12 now, with the September 4 subject to a July go/no-go."

**5. Bilingual attrition isn't modeled.** Reaching 10 bilingual agents against a need of 9 leaves a margin of one. At 38% attrition, you'd expect to lose 3–4 bilingual agents in 2027. "Bilingual preferred" for backfills may not be enough. Consider "bilingual required for backfills until we reach 10."

**6. The vendor shortfall range needs a footnote.** With 42 fully productive agents plus a ramping class, February's gap is ~20k. Once all 50 are fully productive, it's ~14.6k. The 16,000–17,500 range is plausible as a weighted average, but a reader can't reproduce it. One line of derivation would help, as would stating the remaining unmet volume (~12–16k tickets over the season, versus ~28% short each month in 2026).

## Clarity and polish

- **"Dispute tracking and card replacement"** appear for the first time in the September rationale. Name them earlier, or add "(the Q2 self-service launches)."
- **Voice:** The memo is from "Support Operations," but the attrition section says "I will bring a proposal." Pick one.
- **Stray heading:** The document ends with an empty `##` after the horizontal rule. Delete it.
- **Consistency:** You use both "Sept" and "September," and "help-centre" (British) alongside US-style "Jan 11." Choose one style.
- **"Which explains why Spanish waits are 3.4 times longer"** is a fair inference but stated as fact. "Which is the main driver of" is safer.
- **Assumptions list:** Add the 740 tickets/agent/month figure, which drives every agent count, and the $68k loaded cost per agent.

## Bottom line

The analysis is sound and the phasing logic is persuasive. Before sending, I'd fix four things: add the total cost (~$760k), reconcile the off-peak agent figures, make the September approval explicitly conditional, and acknowledge that attrition ramp loss leaves no margin. That last point also strengthens your case for the Q1 attrition proposal.
